detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the right, black shadow.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on a medium close shot of <Subject 1>, bare-headed with his auburn hair blown wild, in the mustard-ochre tweed suit and round steel spectacles, his trousers dark with dew to the knee on the pavement outside the white palings, turned three-quarters toward the camera, both hands gripping the pointed tops, leaning over them into the garden, breathless, sand on his tweed and in his beard. The camera is on the pavement beside him level with his eyes, an arm's length from him, looking along the palings, a 50mm lens. The low sun comes from the RIGHT onto his face. At the first frame Ogilvy's head and shoulders fill the LEFT half of the frame from his wild auburn hair at the TOP third to his gripping hands on the palings at the BOTTOM edge, his head a third of the frame's height. The shot is inside this place: A quiet street in Woking at half past six on an early summer morning in 1894: a waist-high fence of white-painted pointed palings with a wicket gate fronting a small vegetable garden of peas on sticks, lettuces and runner beans on canes, the dug soil dark, a semi-detached yellow-brick villa with a slate roof. The camera keeps a locked-off frame as he leans over the palings and calls out, from 00:00 to 00:06. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, broad ruddy face, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] Henderson! That shooting star: it is out on Horsell Common!</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:06, as the line ends, his hand shakes the pointed tops, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is keeping through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
